frontier_ideas.title: FI-4 Damped-Picard gain criterion for the pipeline's actual outer loop
frontier_ideas.informal_statement:
Let H_λ(T) = (1−λ)T + λ g(T), with g differentiable on an H-invariant box [a, b] and g' ∈ [m, M] there.
- If 1 − 2/λ < m and M < 1, then H_λ is a contraction on the box with rate max(|1−λ+λm|, |1−λ+λM|) < 1, giving a unique fixed point and geometric convergence.
- Conversely, if g(T*) = T* and g'(T*) > 1, then T* is repelling for every λ ∈ (0, 1]: no damping rescues monotone positive feedback.
- For the pipeline's λ = 1/2 the admissible window is g' ∈ (−3, 1).
- Instantiated with R9-02's u-map, whose gain is g' = c·β, this makes c·β ≥ 1 a proven abstention condition.
frontier_ideas.lean_sketch:
def dampedMap (lam : ℝ) (g : ℝ → ℝ) (T : ℝ) : ℝ := (1 - lam) * T + lam * g T
theorem dampedMap_contracts {g g' : ℝ → ℝ} {a b m M lam : ℝ} (hlam : 0 < lam ∧ lam ≤ 1)
  (hd : ∀ T ∈ Set.Icc a b, HasDerivAt g (g' T) T) (hmM : ∀ T ∈ Set.Icc a b, m ≤ g' T ∧ g' T ≤ M)
  (hlo : 1 - 2 / lam < m) (hhi : M < 1) (hmaps : Set.MapsTo (dampedMap lam g) (Set.Icc a b) (Set.Icc a b)) :
  ∃! Tstar, Tstar ∈ Set.Icc a b ∧ dampedMap lam g Tstar = Tstar ∧ ∀ T0 ∈ Set.Icc a b, Filter.Tendsto (fun n => (dampedMap lam g)^[n] T0) Filter.atTop (nhds Tstar)
theorem dampedMap_repelling {g : ℝ → ℝ} {d Tstar lam : ℝ} (hfix : g Tstar = Tstar) (hd : HasDerivAt g d Tstar) (hd1 : 1 < d) (hlam : 0 < lam) : ∃ ε > 0, ∀ T, 0 < |T - Tstar| → |T - Tstar| < ε → |T - Tstar| < |dampedMap lam g T - Tstar|

frontier_ideas.title: FI-2 Energy-affine atomic-data gauge: the calibration-layer non-identifiability theorem
frontier_ideas.informal_statement: Suppose the tabulated A' satisfy log(A_k/A'_k) = α + b·E_k, affine in the upper-level energy. Then the fitted Boltzmann slope equals −1/(kT) + b exactly, and the least-squares residual is unchanged (zero on-manifold). The data are thus observationally identical to the true data at a shifted temperature T', 1/(kT') = 1/(kT) − b, plus an intercept shift. With a per-spectrum free T and a free Fcal, the E-linear component b of a global per-line correction δ_l is exactly unidentifiable within one stage and one U-family. In multi-species or multi-stage data it leaks into composition only through U_s(T')/U_s(T) and the Saha T-terms, bounded by PartitionLipschitz.

  leastSquaresResidual E (fun k => Real.log (lineIntensity kB T N Fcal g E A k / (g k * A' k))) = 0

frontier_ideas.title: FI-5 Weighted least squares (Aitken) optimality and weighted Fisher monotonicity
frontier_ideas.informal_statement: Under uncorrelated heteroscedastic noise Var ε_k = σ_k², the WLS slope with w_k = 1/σ_k² is the best linear unbiased estimator, with Var = 1/Σ_k w_k (E_k − Ē_w)². The OLS slope variance Σ_k (w^ols_k)² σ_k² can strictly exceed it. Adding a line never increases the WLS variance (the weighted spreadOn_insert analogue). An explicit counterexample shows that adding one very noisy line can increase the OLS variance, so FisherLineSelection's "adding a line never hurts" is a WLS/homoscedastic fact only.

frontier_ideas.title: FI-6 Linear line extraction under profile misspecification: exact bias identity and bound
frontier_ideas.informal_statement: Model pixel data as y = K_true·I + ε. The extractor is Î = (KᵀK)⁻¹Kᵀy, built from an assumed profile matrix K (spec 03 §3 K5). Exactly, Î − I = (KᵀK)⁻¹Kᵀ(K_true − K)·I + (KᵀK)⁻¹Kᵀε. Hence ‖bias‖ ≤ ‖(KᵀK)⁻¹Kᵀ‖·‖K_true − K‖·‖I‖, and Cov Î = σ²(KᵀK)⁻¹ for white noise. When K is built at the true state (the benchmark's oracle extractor), the bias term vanishes identically. So the oracle's accuracy says nothing about the shipped extractor, whose error is exactly the LSF, Stark-width×n_e and shift error propagated through (KᵀK)⁻¹Kᵀ.

theorem extractor_bias_identity {P L : Type*} [Fintype P] [Fintype L] [DecidableEq L] (K Kt : Matrix P L ℝ) (I : L → ℝ) (ε : P → ℝ) (hdet : (Kᵀ * K).det ≠ 0) :
  ((Kᵀ * K)⁻¹ * Kᵀ).mulVec (Kt.mulVec I + ε) - I = ((Kᵀ * K)⁻¹ * Kᵀ).mulVec ((Kt - K).mulVec I) + ((Kᵀ * K)⁻¹ * Kᵀ).mulVec ε
theorem extractor_exact_of_true_profile (hdet) : ((Kᵀ * K)⁻¹ * Kᵀ).mulVec (K.mulVec I) = I
theorem extractor_bias_le (hdet) : ‖bias‖ ≤ ‖(Kᵀ * K)⁻¹ * Kᵀ‖ * ‖Kt - K‖ * ‖I‖  -- with Matrix.linftyOpNorm

summary:
Literature slice, re-verified after the session restart. Every citation below was retrieved this session (Semantic Scholar through the asta CLI; raw JSON is in docs/research/audit-2026-09-24/evidence/lit/) or comes from the verified files. The spec is honest about what it models. Its literature gaps fall into three groups.
(1) Physics the literature uses and the spec never states. Ionization-potential depression (IPD) is absent: there is no Lean object, and the M4 acceptance doc wrongly calls IPD 'fine'. There are no results on how temperature splits between charge stages, or on the sign of the temperature bias that self-absorption causes; the literature disagrees on that sign. The spec also has no mass-fraction bridge, although the pipeline is scored in wt%.
(2) Error bounds too loose to test the literature's informal claims. The closure chain (C6, classicComposition_atomicData_error, noise_to_composition) turns relative per-species errors into one absolute bound, so it can neither confirm nor refute Gornushkin & Völker's 2022 claim that closure amplifies errors on minor elements. For a 0.5% minor element with a 5% atomic-data error, the repo bound is 0.0557: 11 times the fraction itself and about 106 times the true worst case of 5.2e-4.
(3) Citation errors of the kind the repo has been hurt by before. A real title is credited to the wrong authors: the IntechOpen chapter is by F. Rezaei (2016), not Aragón & Aguilera. The title given for JQSRT 149 (2014) 90 has no Semantic Scholar record. The corrigendum volume is wrong (155; it is 159). The source for ForwardMapEnergy is Thouin et al., so the reviews that name 'Khelladi' are wrong. The whitelist has zero rows with first-hand evidence, because its one CORRECTED row admits the source was never opened.
Two search negatives, each with a positive control. (a) No prior machine-checked formalization of CF-LIBS was found. The snippet search for formal proofs and identifiability in CF-LIBS returned only formal-identifiability papers from other fields, which shows the search ran. (b) The literature's informal claims on identifiability, bias direction and closure propagation are mostly unproved in the repo. InhomogeneityBias is the exception: it proves the one-stage mixing sign, and it credits Craig & Brown as prior art.
The six frontier ideas are all new; each was checked by grep over CflibsFormal/ and docs/frontiers. FI-1 to FI-3 type-check with sorry against the built repo (docs/research/audit-2026-09-24/evidence/lit/Frontier.lean). FI-4 to FI-6 have prose sketches only. The full payload is mirrored at docs/research/audit-2026-09-24/evidence/lit/structured_output.json.

Pipeline: partition.py:81-95 computes Debye-Hückel Δχ = Z·e²/λ_D with λ_D = sqrt(kT/(4π n_e e²)), 'the Saha exponent and the direct-sum partition cutoff use one consistent Δχ'. partition.py:166 and :207 sum 'U(T) = Σ gᵢ exp(-Eᵢ/kT) for Eᵢ < IP - Δχ' with e_max = ip_ev - delta_chi. ipd.py implements Stewart–Pyatt. The overhaul records IPD 'on in the forward and off in the inverse, so n_e comes out 0.936× low' (review-summary.md:32) and 'IPD adds positive feedback' to the n_e runaway (review-summary.md:68); see also BL-42 and BL-37.
Literature (retrieved): Ristić, Krstevski, Ranković, Marković, Šajić, Kuzmanović 2024, 'The influence of continuum lowering on the equilibrium composition of plasma: case study of laser-induced plasma on a WC–Cu target', Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion, DOI 10.1088/1361-6587/ad8b68. Abstract: 'the correction to the partition functions due to the reduction of the ionization potential is of greater importance than the correction to the Boltzmann term at higher temperatures for atomic species'.

findings.claim: The M4 acceptance doc says: 'An IPD-lowered χ − Δχ is fine, provided forward and inverse use the same value.' This is an overclaim. In the pipeline Δχ depends on n_e and T, and the level cutoff moves with it. The T-grid monotonicity and Lipschitz rows, the closed-form n_e inversion, and the contraction certificates C9/C10 therefore do not transfer to an IPD-on context.
findings.recommendation: Amend cross-cutting condition 2 in the doc. IPD transfers only pointwise, at a fixed (n_e, T) with a fixed level list. The T-grid, Lipschitz and enclosure rows, and C9/C10, are NOT acceptance criteria for an IPD-on PopulationContext. Add IPD-specific rows once FI-4 exists. Cross-reference the doc to BL-40 and BL-42.

findings.claim: The IntechOpen chapter is attributed to the wrong authors. The module credits 'Optically Thick Laser-Induced Plasmas in Spectroscopic Analysis' to Aragón & Aguilera and cites its Eqs. 19/20 and 29–31. The chapter is by F. Rezaei (2016). This is the failure class the repo ranks worst: a real title attached to the wrong authors.

asta papers get DOI:10.5772/61941 returns the title 'Optically Thick Laser-Induced Plasmas in Spectroscopic Analysis', author F. Rezaei, year 2016, publicationDate 2016-04-20, CorpusId 53339271. Otherwise cite the slope-½ wing to Ladenburg–Reiche 1913 (already whitelisted) or Gornushkin 1999. Update whitelist row 71.

findings.claim: The closure-error chain is advertised as the per-element reliability deliverable for many-element alloys, but it is abundance-blind. Relative per-species errors (atomic data, temperature response) are collapsed into one absolute δ = Nmax·δ_rel/(1−δ_rel). The resulting bounds are vacuous for minor elements, and they cannot confirm or refute the literature's claim that closure amplifies errors on minor elements.
findings.recommendation: Prove FI-3, i.e. relative bounds that scale with abundance. Restate classicComposition_atomicData_error and noise_to_composition in relative form, since their hypotheses are already relative. Add a relative-tolerance variant of C6. Until then, qualify the docstrings: the bounds are informative only for species with C_s comparable to Nmax/Ŝ.

findings.claim: Measured along the line of sight, neutral and ionic Boltzmann plots give DIFFERENT apparent temperatures. The Cσ and Saha–Boltzmann modules put both stages on one slope, and have no caveat about homogeneity. InhomogeneityBias bounds only one stage at a time, so the neutral/ion split is unmodelled. The pipeline's pooled SB-graph slope inherits this.
findings.evidence:
Retrieved: Aguilera & Aragón 2007, 'Apparent excitation temperature in laser-induced plasmas', J. Phys.: Conf. Ser. 59:210-217, DOI 10.1088/1742-6596/59/1/046. From the abstract: 'the values of the apparent temperature obtained for neutral atoms and ions are different … apparent temperatures for neutral atoms (9890 K) and ions (11400 K)'.
Spec: InhomogeneityBias builds weights for one species only (zoneWeight w z = Fcal·N z/U(T_z), :488-491). CSigma.lean:27-30 collapses ionic lines onto 'the SAME master line'. rg 'inhomogen|homogeneous|single temperature|one temperature|isotherm' over Alt/CSigma.lean, SahaInverse.lean and Alt/CSigmaCurveOfGrowth.lean returns 0 hits; the same pattern hits in InhomogeneityBias.lean, so it runs.
Pipeline: overhaul R9-performance.md:36, 'The SB-graph fit uses … a fixed design [x | element dummies]. Ion rows get x=E_k+IP_eff'. That is one slope across stages.
The string 'Aguilera & Aragón 2007' in the repo already means Spectrochim. Acta B 62:378, so the JPCS paper needs a distinct string.
findings.recommendation: Prove FI-1. Add a homogeneity caveat to the Alt/CSigma, SahaInverse and CSigmaCurveOfGrowth docstrings: a cross-stage collapse assumes one T, and line-of-sight integration generically breaks it. Whitelist the JPCS paper as 'Aguilera & Aragón 2007b (JPCS)'.

findings.claim: The spec proves that self-absorption biases intensity and density downward. It never states the sign of the temperature (Boltzmann-slope) bias that uncorrected self-absorption causes. The literature disagrees on that sign.
findings.evidence:
Spec: the proven bias directions are intensity/density only: thickLineIntensity_lt_lineIntensity_of_pos_density (OpticalDepthBridge.lean:35) and selfAbsorbed_corrects_bias (Alt/SelfAbsorbed.lean:112-118, 'underestimates density'). Temperature is addressed only as 'τ/I_thin antitone in T' (OpticalDepth.lean:60-64). SelfAbsorption.lean:240-248 treats correction with a known τ as exact. No SA module relates selfAbsorptionFactor to olsSlope, pairSlope or twoLineBeta; the only co-occurrence is DifferentialEstimator, which assumes matched τ.
Literature (retrieved), split on the sign:
- John & Anoop 2023, RSC Adv., DOI 10.1039/d3ra06226k (simulation): 'With self-absorption the temperature calculated using Boltzmann plot has significantly diverged from the simulated temperature (Ca I 1.00 eV, Ca II 1.48 eV, Mg I 1.04 eV, and Mg II 1.48 eV)', against a true 1 eV.
- Fayyaz et al. 2024, Anal. Sci. 40:413, DOI 10.1007/s44211-023-00480-9: self-absorption 'can lead to an underestimation of element concentrations and temperature measurements'.
- Safi et al. 2019, J. Adv. Res. 18:1, DOI 10.1016/j.jare.2019.01.008: low-lying levels 'more prone to self-absorption, resulting in an inaccurate estimation of the plasma temperature'.
findings.recommendation: Prove FI-2: T is overestimated whenever τ is antitone in E_upper, the resonance-line ordering. Add a two-line counterexample with the opposite ordering, which settles the sign dispute conditionally. Note the result in the OpticalDepth and SelfAbsorption scope sections.

findings.claim: The spec declines to use the El Sherbini width/self-absorption power law, and says no bibliographic record for it is asserted. The record exists. Under the module's own homogeneous-Lorentzian slab model, the relation also holds within a narrow exponent band, so it could be proved rather than refused. The pipeline inverts widths with exponent 0.56, which the spec could anchor.
findings.evidence:
OpacityBroadening.lean:87-91: 'w_obs = w_Stark · SA^(−0.54) … deliberately not used here and no bibliographic record for it is asserted'.
Retrieved: El Sherbini, El Sherbini, Hegazy, Cristoforetti, Legnaioli, Palleschi 2005, 'Evaluation of self-absorption coefficients of aluminum emission lines in LIBS measurements', DOI 10.1016/J.SAB.2005.10.011 (285 citations). Safi et al. 2019 (DOI 10.1016/j.jare.2019.01.008) quotes 'a = −0.54 for Lorentzian line profiles'.
Computation with the module's exact ratio lorentzWidthRatio τ = sqrt(1/h(τ) − 1), where h(τ) = −ln((1+e^−τ)/2)/τ and SA(τ) = (1−e^−τ)/τ. The effective exponent ln R/(−ln SA), evaluated on 20001 log-spaced τ in [1e-4, 1e4], lies in (0.5000, 0.5687] with its maximum at τ ≈ 5.2. Sample values: 0.534 at τ=1, 0.554 at τ=2, 0.539 at τ=100. The limit is 1/2 at both ends.
Pipeline: opc.py:855-856 sets 'CDSB_COG_EXP: float = 0.56' in dl/dl0 = ((1-e^-kl)/kl)^-0.56 and inverts it up to kl = 50 (CDSB_KL_MAX).
findings.recommendation: Replace the refusal with FI-6: a proven band SA^(−1/2) ≤ R(τ) ≤ SA^(−0.57), and hence a certified bracket that turns a measured width ratio into an SA value. Cite El Sherbini 2005 by DOI with status UNVERIFIED until the paper is opened.

findings.claim: Optical-depth recovery from a doublet or curve of growth is proved injective and continuous, but there is no conditioning or modulus bound. The literature's central objection concerns conditioning, not injectivity, and the spec does not cite it.
findings.evidence:
Present: doubletRatio_injOn (:248), doublet_fit_unique (:353), doubletRatio_continuousOn (:395), cogRatio_injOn (CurveOfGrowth.lean:254). rg 'lipschitz|stab|condition|sensitiv' over both files finds no inverse-modulus result. The docstring at :86-90 admits the attainable range 'is not characterized'. The doublet ratio tends to 1 as τ→∞, so δτ grows like e^τ·δD.
Retrieved: Maali & Shabanov 2019, 'Error analysis in optimization problems relevant for CF-LIBS', JQSRT, DOI 10.1016/J.JQSRT.2018.10.029: 'relative uncertainties in the values of the spectral parameters … cannot be made small because there exist large (correlated) variations … under which the fit error remains less than a preassigned (small) value', for τ from 1e-4 to 1e2. rg 'Maali|Shabanov' over the repo finds nothing.

frontier_ideas.title: FI-1: ion apparent temperature ≥ neutral apparent temperature (Saha reweighting of the tilted mean)
frontier_ideas.informal_statement: Take a plasma that is a positive mixture of LTE zones with uniform n_e, measured along the line of sight. Ion-stage zone weights equal neutral-stage weights times ρ_z = 2Λ(T_z)^{3/2}·exp(−χ b_z)/n_e. The partition functions cancel exactly, and ρ is antitone in b_z = 1/(k T_z). A reweighting antitone in b lowers the tilted mean inverse temperature at any fixed anchor, and tiltMean is antitone in the anchor. Hence, if the ion pair's lower line energy is at least the neutral pair's upper line energy, β_app(ion) ≤ β_app(neutral), so T_app(ion) ≥ T_app(neutral). This proves the sign that Aguilera & Aragón (2007) measured.
frontier_ideas.lean_sketch:
theorem tiltMean_reweight_le [Nonempty ζ] {w b ρ : ζ → ℝ} (hw : ∀ z, 0 < w z) (hρ : ∀ z, 0 < ρ z) (hanti : ∀ i j, b i ≤ b j → ρ j ≤ ρ i) (a : ℝ) : tiltMean (fun z => w z * ρ z) b a ≤ tiltMean w b a  -- type-checks with sorry in Frontier.lean.
Corollary mixed_ion_apparentBeta_le_neutral: from mixed_apparentBeta_le_tiltMean (ion stage, anchor E_lo^II), tiltMean_reweight_le, tiltMean antitone in the anchor (via tiltMean_le_pairSlope and pairSlope_le_tiltMean), and tiltMean_le_pairSlope (neutral stage, anchor E_up^I), under the hypothesis E_up^I ≤ E_lo^II.
frontier_ideas.why_it_matters: It turns the standard observation that ion Boltzmann plots run hotter into a theorem with explicit hypotheses, namely uniform n_e and the anchor ordering. It shows that the cross-stage collapse in Cσ/Saha–Boltzmann, and the pipeline's pooled SB-graph slope, mixes two different tilted means. The single-T identifiability of saha_joint_identifiability has no counterpart in a mixed plasma.
frontier_ideas.pipeline_link: LIT-06; overhaul R9-performance.md:36 (pooled SB-graph slope with ion rows at x = E_k + IP_eff); G2-gap-fill.md:53 (the T_saha consistency diagnostic is tautological); M8 per-element flags
frontier_ideas.literature: Aguilera & Aragón 2007, 'Apparent excitation temperature in laser-induced plasmas', J. Phys.: Conf. frontier_ideas.title: FI-2: self-absorption flattens the OLS Boltzmann slope when τ is antitone in the upper-level energy
frontier_ideas.informal_statement: Suppose optical depth decreases with upper-level energy, as for resonance and low-lying lines. Then the OLS slope of the self-absorbed Boltzmann plot is at least the thin-plasma slope. With the repo's raw ordinate (slope = −1/(kT) < 0), the slope moves toward zero, so the apparent temperature is an overestimate while the slope stays negative. With the opposite ordering, a two-line counterexample shows the sign flips. Together these settle the literature's disagreement conditionally.
frontier_ideas.lean_sketch:
theorem olsSlope_selfAbsorbed_ge [Nonempty ι] {E y τ : ι → ℝ} (hτ : ∀ k, 0 < τ k) (hanti : ∀ i j, E i ≤ E j → τ j ≤ τ i) : olsSlope E y ≤ olsSlope E (fun k => y k + Real.log (selfAbsorptionFactor (τ k)))  -- type-checks with sorry in Frontier.lean.
Proof: olsSlope is linear in y (olsSlope_eq_centered, OLS.lean:87). Real.log ∘ SA is antitone on (0,∞) (selfAbsorptionFactor_strictAntiOn, SelfAbsorption.lean:106, and Real.log_le_log), so the added term monovaries with E. Then Σ(E−Ē)(f−f̄) ≥ 0 by Chebyshev.
Plus: example with τ increasing in E and a strict decrease.
frontier_ideas.why_it_matters: The literature asserts both signs. John & Anoop 2023 simulate a temperature overestimate; Fayyaz 2024 states an underestimate. The spec currently proves only intensity and density directions. Temperature drives every downstream quantity, and self-absorption correction is opt-in in the pipeline.

frontier_ideas.title: FI-3: the closure relative-error dichotomy: closure is abundance-neutral, and amplification on minors comes from the error model
frontier_ideas.informal_statement: (a) If every species' density has a multiplicative error |N̂_s/N_s − 1| ≤ η < 1, then |Ĉ_s − C_s| ≤ (2η/(1−η))·C_s for EVERY s, whatever the abundance. The same holds for mass fractions, since reweighting by atomic mass preserves multiplicative errors. (b) For an additive per-species error δ, a witness shows relative error at least of order δ/N_s. So the amplification on minors that Gornushkin & Völker attribute to summation comes from additive error components, not from the normalization.
frontier_ideas.why_it_matters: It replaces the abundance-blind bounds of LIT-05. Those bounds are 11 times the fraction for a 0.5% minor; the new bound is tight, at 5.3e-4 against an actual 5.2e-4. It also turns an informal literature claim into a precise dichotomy, and it gives M8 per-element flags and C6 a relative-tolerance form that transfers to wt% (LIT-14).

frontier_ideas.title: FI-4: IPD-aware Saha inversion: at most one physical n_e root, and inner-iteration contraction at rate Δχ/(2kT)
frontier_ideas.informal_statement: Take Debye–Hückel lowering Δχ(n_e, T) = kT·a(T)·sqrt(n_e). The Saha condition R·n_e = S0(T)·exp(Δχ/kT) has at most two positive roots, because in y = ln n_e the map h(y) = y − ln(S0/R) − a·e^{y/2} is strictly concave. At most one root satisfies Δχ < 2kT. At a fixed point, the inner iteration n ↦ S0·e^{Δχ(n)/kT}/R has log-derivative exactly Δχ/(2kT). So it contracts locally if and only if Δχ < 2kT, and it contracts globally on {y ≤ y_c} whenever F(y_c) ≤ y_c and Δχ(e^{y_c}) < 2kT. The general form requires the elasticity n·∂Δχ/∂n < kT. (This condition is the auditor's own derivation, not taken from the literature.)
frontier_ideas.why_it_matters: It is the first spec object for IPD (LIT-01), and it gives a checkable certificate for the pipeline's IPD-on inner n_e loop. With the pipeline's own figures (Δχ ≈ 0.066 eV at 1e17 cm⁻³ and 1e4 K, against 2kT ≈ 1.72 eV) the rate is ≈ 0.04, which certifies the three-inner-step jit loop in the normal regime. By the √n_e scaling the condition fails only near n_e ~ 7e19 cm⁻³ at 1e4 K, i.e. at early dense gates. It also explains why a spurious high-n_e root can exist.

frontier_ideas.title: FI-5: duplicating-mirror channel: τ from a single line, plus over-determination that gives DoubletChannel its missing model-adequacy test
frontier_ideas.informal_statement: Model assumption, stated abstractly and not taken from Moon 2009's equations: a mirror of known effective reflectivity R_m sends the slab emission back through the same homogeneous slab, so the second observable is I_M = I·(1 + R_m·e^{−τ}). (a) Given R_m, τ = −ln((I_M/I − 1)/R_m) is identifiable from ONE line, which removes single_line_tau_alias. (b) With a doublet, there are three observables and two unknowns (F, τ). Any homogeneous slab has zero residual, while the two-zone emitter of inhomogeneous_doublet_admits_exact_homogeneous_fit has generically nonzero residual. That yields the over-determined model-adequacy test DoubletChannel says it lacks.
frontier_ideas.why_it_matters: It gives the first over-determined self-absorption observable in the spec, which turns the doublet channel's admitted blindness into a checkable consistency certificate. The single-line part is closed-form, so it is directly usable as a runtime certificate.

frontier_ideas.title: FI-6: El Sherbini exponent band: SA(τ)^(−1/2) ≤ Lorentzian width ratio ≤ SA(τ)^(−0.57)
frontier_ideas.informal_statement: For the module's homogeneous Lorentzian slab, the exact emergent-width inflation R(τ) = sqrt(1/h(τ) − 1) satisfies SA^(−1/2) < R ≤ SA^(−0.569) for all τ > 0. The auditor's numerics give an effective exponent in (0.5000, 0.5687], peaking near τ ≈ 5.2 and tending to 1/2 at both ends. So a measured width ratio brackets the self-absorption factor: R^(−2) ≤ SA ≤ R^(−1/0.57). The literature's −0.54 and the pipeline's 0.56 both fall inside the proven band.

summary: I checked all 13 frontier dossiers and the ROADMAP against the code at fb1681d. Every deliverable the ROADMAP marks ✅ exists: I grepped 60 declaration names across frontiers 01–12 and none is missing. The refusals are where the status is wrong. The mathlib inventories were stamped "grep-verified v4.31.0", but two of their ABSENT or "not readily available" claims were false when written; `git merge-base` confirms the lemmas are in v4.31.0. Frontier 03's Newton step (M8) was refused as "concave-Newton infra ABSENT", yet `convexOn_zpow` has been in mathlib since 2023, and Newton needs no convexity library at all: I proved its exact error identity axiom-clean in about 30 lines of `field_simp`/`nlinarith` in scratch. Frontier 11 refused the exact Gaussian law of the fitted slope β̂ because a Gaussian-closure lemma was thought missing, but `iIndepFun.hasGaussianLaw` and `HasGaussianLaw.map_eq_gaussianReal` are both in v4.31.0; I proved that any weighted sum of independent Gaussian noises has an identified Gaussian law in about 15 lines. Three more status items are stale. LineBroadening "asserts" the Gaussian-quadrature width rule, which mathlib's `gaussianReal_conv_gaussianReal` together with two lemmas I proved turns into an EXACT theorem. Dossier 12's grade-C "a-priori n_e box for C11" is now discharged by `electronDensityFromRatio_mem_Icc`. Frontier 04 is marked ✅ with no simultaneous witness, and its positive slope floor is not tied to the sign-normalized convention in its docstrings. In the dev spec, Phase 6 needs a quantitative instrument-kernel error gain that Phase 3 explicitly refuses to predict. Scenario 7(b), Gaussian lines on top-hat pixels, cannot have a Float mirror because neither mathlib nor Lean's Float has erf; Lorentzian lines can, using `integral_inv_one_add_sq` and `Float.atan`. Present in mathlib v4.33.1: Cauchy and Gaussian densities and their integrals, `integral_convolution`, measure convolution with a probability-measure instance, `ContractingWith` with a-priori and a-posteriori bounds, the intermediate and implicit function theorems, convexity of zpow, variance and Chebyshev, sub-Gaussian bounds and Hoeffding, Gaussian-law closure, an asymptotic CLT, `Matrix.rank`, Gershgorin (det≠0 and eigenvalue balls), and the spectral theorem. Absent: erf/Faddeeva, modified Bessel functions, Fisher information and Cramér–Rao, a matrix condition number, Berry–Esseen, a strict Chebyshev sum inequality, the Cauchy characteristic function, and `Float.erf`. On Worker capability, the queue verified Frontier 02 in 1.9 h, but Frontier 07, a dominated-convergence measure-theory target, failed at its 300k-token cap. So the algebraic ideas below (A) are safe Worker targets, and the analysis-heavy ones (B) need finer decomposition. The scratch proofs are in `docs/research/audit-2026-09-24/evidence/frontier-mathlib/`: `Newton.lean`, `Quad.lean`, `Varah.lean`, `GLaw.lean` and `Sketch.lean`, all type-checked with `lake env lean`. The four proofs depend only on {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}.

findings.claim: The Frontier 03 M8 Newton refusal rests on a false mathlib-absence claim and on a false belief that convexity machinery is needed.
findings.evidence: ROADMAP.md:147 says: "03 M8 | Newton quadratic rate | **REFUSED — not attempted** (concave-Newton convexity infra ABSENT; §5: defer indefinitely)". 03:191 says: "Convexity of `x ↦ (x+S)⁻¹` ... ABSENT as a ready lemma — `convexOn_rpow` requires `p ≥ 1`". In fact mathlib Analysis/Convex/Mul.lean:177 has `lemma convexOn_zpow : ∀ n : ℤ, ConvexOn 𝕜 (Ioi 0) fun x ↦ x ^ n`, added in commit 54f7158db9 (2023-11-24), and SpecificFunctions/Deriv.lean:99 has `strictConvexOn_zpow`; `git merge-base --is-ancestor` shows both are in tag v4.31.0. More decisively, I proved the exact Newton error identity `N x − r = −((x−r)²·∑ Ntot·S/((x+S)²(r+S)))/(1+∑ Ntot·S/(x+S)²)` directly from `multiElementIonized_two_point` with `field_simp`/`nlinarith`, no convexity lemma involved. Scratch file: docs/research/audit-2026-09-24/evidence/frontier-mathlib/Newton.lean; `#print axioms` gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. `rg -i newton CflibsFormal` returns 0 hits (positive control: 17 hits in docs/frontiers).
findings.recommendation: Retract the M8 refusal in ROADMAP §3, the Phase 3 table and §5, and in dossier 03 §3/§4. Re-grade M8 from C to A. Queue the Newton ladder (frontier idea 1) on the Worker.

findings.claim: Frontier 11 refused the exact Gaussian law of β̂ on a premise that was already false in its own pinned mathlib.
findings.evidence: 11:476-481 says: "the 'linear combination of independent Gaussians is Gaussian' closure lemma for a general finite weighted sum is not readily available (convolution-of-Gaussians is thin), so this is a large, separate infrastructure project". The needed lemmas exist: mathlib has `iIndepFun.hasGaussianLaw` (Gaussian/HasGaussianLaw/Independence.lean:171, commit b8a2460549, 2026-01-27), `HasGaussianLaw.map_of_measurable` (HasGaussianLaw/Basic.lean:70), `HasGaussianLaw.map_eq_gaussianReal` (:80) and `gaussianReal_conv_gaussianReal` (Gaussian/Real.lean:645, 2025-05-19). All are ancestors of tag v4.31.0. I proved `weightedNoise_map_eq`, which identifies μ.map(∑ w_k ε_k) as gaussianReal(mean, Var), in about 15 lines; it is axiom-clean (scratch GLaw.lean). The dossier's TRAP bullet (sub-Gaussian needs iIndepFun, not mere uncorrelation) is partly dissolved by `HasGaussianLaw.iIndepFun_of_covariance_eq_zero` (Independence.lean:261): jointly Gaussian and uncorrelated noise is independent. My Sketch.lean `example` using it type-checks.

Add a dossier note that the exact finite-sample interval under a Gaussian noise model is not CLT-based, so the CLT refusal (which stands, since Berry–Esseen is still absent) does not cover it. Fix the inventory row claiming the closure lemma is ABSENT.

findings.claim: The Gaussian-quadrature width rule is a bare definition labelled "exact" and "asserted", although it has been provable from mathlib since v4.31.0.
findings.evidence: LineBroadening.lean:27 says: "Honesty: the Gaussian-quadrature law is **exact** for Gaussian⊗Gaussian convolution (asserted here as the operational width rule, the standard consequence of `gaussian ⋆ gaussian = gaussian`)". `gaussQuadrature` (line 98) is only `Real.sqrt (w₁ ^ 2 + w₂ ^ 2)`, and no theorem links it to any convolution: rg for `gaussianReal|HasGaussianLaw|convolution` in CflibsFormal code finds 0 statements. mathlib has `gaussianReal_conv_gaussianReal : gaussianReal m₁ v₁ ∗ gaussianReal m₂ v₂ = gaussianReal (m₁+m₂) (v₁+v₂)`. I proved `gaussFWHM_conv : gaussFWHM (v₁+v₂) = gaussQuadrature (gaussFWHM v₁) (gaussFWHM v₂)` and `gaussianPDFReal_halfMax` (pdf at μ₀ + FWHM/2 equals half the peak); both are axiom-clean (scratch Quad.lean). VoigtWidth.lean:15 builds on the same asserted rule.

findings.claim: Frontier 04 is marked closed (✅) with no joint-satisfiability witness, and the combined-slope definition requires the sign-normalized ordinate without saying so.
findings.evidence: OuterLoopModelB.lean:47 says: "No concrete end-to-end witness satisfying all hypotheses simultaneously is constructed here". `hslopeFloor` demands `0 < smin ≤ combinedSahaBoltzmannSlope …`, and `combinedSlopeTempUpdate = 1/(kB·slope)`. The repo's physical Boltzmann plot has a negative slope: Alt/LeastSquares.lean:97 says `= -(1 / (kB * T)) * E k + Real.log (...)`. StochasticBudget.lean explicitly works on the "sign-normalized branch β = 1/(k_B·T)", but the `combinedSahaBoltzmannSlope` docstring (ErrorBudget.lean:484-492) never says that y and the Saha offset `(offConst − log ne)·s k` must be in that convention. frontier_ideas.title: Newton's method on the charge-neutrality equation: exact error identity, certified bracket, global quadratic convergence (reopens Frontier 03 M8)
frontier_ideas.informal_statement: For G(x)=∑_s Ntot_s S_s/(x+S_s) with fixed point r, the Newton map N(x)=x−(x−G x)/(1+∑ Ntot_s S_s/(x+S_s)²) has the closed form (∑ a_s(2x+S_s)/(x+S_s)²)/(1+∑ a_s/(x+S_s)²), where a_s = Ntot_s S_s, so N x > 0. It satisfies the exact identity N x − r = −(x−r)²·∑ a_s/((x+S_s)²(r+S_s)) / f'(x). Consequences: N x ≤ r always; x ≤ N x whenever x ≤ r; |N x − r| ≤ (∑ Ntot_s/S_s²)(x−r)²; and every iterate after the first gives the certified bracket x_n ≤ r ≤ G(x_n). The iteration converges from every x₀ ≥ 0, at a linear rate r/(r+min S) and eventually quadratically.

frontier_ideas.informal_statement: If the per-line log-intensity noises ε_k are independent N(0,σ²), then β̂ ~ N(β, σ²/SS_E) exactly, so μ{|β̂−β| < z·σ/√SS_E} = N(0,1)(−z,z) exactly for every z. frontier_ideas.title: Gaussian width budget as a theorem, and Voigt as a probability measure (upgrade of spec ContinuousProfile G/V blocks)

Its density falls to half its peak exactly at distance gaussQuadrature(FWHM₁, FWHM₂)/2 from the centre. So LineBroadening's quadrature and deconvolution rules are exact theorems about convolution, not asserted rules. Voigt := Cauchy ∗ Gaussian is a probability measure by instance, and its density is the spec's function-level `voigtProfile`.

frontier_ideas.title: Sharp Doppler (Gaussian) curve-of-growth asymptotic on the flat part: W(τ)/√(ln τ) → 2 (the Gaussian twin of Frontier 07)
frontier_ideas.informal_statement: For the Gaussian absorption profile e^{−x²}, the equivalent width W(τ) = ∫(1−exp(−τ e^{−x²}))dx satisfies W(τ)/√(ln τ) → 2 as τ→∞. Hence on the flat part a relative error in W is amplified by about 2 ln τ in the recovered column density. That quantifies the non-identifiability of the flat part, compared with a factor of 2 in the damping regime (Frontier 07) and 1 in the linear regime.
frontier_ideas.lean_sketch:
theorem equivWidth_gaussian_sqrtLog_sharp : Tendsto (fun τ => equivWidth (fun x => Real.exp (-x ^ 2)) τ / Real.sqrt (Real.log τ)) atTop (𝓝 2)  (statement type-checks, Sketch.lean)
D1 equivWidth_gaussian_scaled (1 < τ): W(τ) = √(ln τ)·∫ u, (1 − exp(−τ^(1−u²))) (substitute x = √(ln τ)·u; integral_comp_mul_left, Real.rpow_def_of_pos)
D2 pointwise: Tendsto (1 − exp(−τ^(1−u²))) atTop (𝓝 (indicator (Ioo (−1) 1) 1 u)) for |u| ≠ 1
D3 domination: e ≤ τ → 0 ≤ integrand ≤ Real.exp 1 * Real.exp (−u²)
D4 DCT: tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence with ∀ᵐ (u ≠ ±1 null) → limit ∫ indicator = 2 (volume_Ioo)
D5 assemble D1+D4 (eventually-equal on (1,∞))
D6 optional corollary: for any ε>0, W(τ)/τ^ε → 0 (flat part is sub-polynomial)

frontier_ideas.title: Varah ℓ∞ noise gain for the instrument kernel (spec K8), with a margin certificate C16′ feeding the composition error chain
frontier_ideas.informal_statement: If the normal matrix KᵀK is strictly row-diagonally dominant with margin δ > 0, then every solution satisfies |x_i| ≤ max_k |(KᵀK x)_k|/δ. So line intensities recovered from pixel sums with noise η satisfy ‖Î−I‖∞ ≤ ‖Kᵀη‖∞/δ. With a positive intensity floor and the existing log-transfer lemma, this becomes a per-line ordinate error ε that plugs straight into `noise_to_composition`.

frontier_ideas.title: Outer-loop certificate C11: a-priori n_e box discharged, plus an a-posteriori error bound for capped iterates
frontier_ideas.informal_statement: On a temperature box, the Saha density leg maps into [n_e(Tmin), n_e(Tmax)] automatically (already proved), so `outerLoop_contracts` needs only the T-leg invariance and the slope floor. Any iterate T, including one stopped at an iteration cap, satisfies |T − T⋆| ≤ |T − Φ(T)|/(1 − L₁L₂). A run that stops at a cap with a small residual therefore has a certified distance to the unique self-consistent temperature.
